patients.summary: College cross-country runner with sickle cell trait who joined the practice at 20. Two exertional heat strokes with rhabdomyolysis (a race in 2024, a summer festival in 2025 with AKI), then a first tonic-clonic seizure with rhabdomyolysis and AKI admitted in April 2026; neurology referral still open.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a student starting the fall term locally, family lives out east. Wants a doctor nearby instead of driving home for everything. Has the student health plan through school. Needs a sports physical form done before team practice starts. Booked new patient physical 8/23 at 9:00. Asked him to bring his athletics packet and any old shot records he can find.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20M, new to us. Starting classes here this fall, runs cross-country for the college (D-II). Needs his pre-participation exam signed.

No complaints. Trains 50-60 miles a week in season. No chest pain, fainting or palpitations with running, no exertional shortness of breath beyond what he'd expect. No prior heat illness or collapse. No concussions.

PMH: sickle cell trait, he says it was picked up on his newborn screen; never any pain crises, blood in the urine or problems with it. Was told by his pediatrician to drink plenty when training.
PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father has sickle cell trait. Mother with high blood pressure. An uncle on dad's side has type 2 diabetes. No sudden deaths in the family that he knows of.
Social: full-time undergrad, lives in an apartment with two teammates. Never smoked, no vaping, does not drink, no drugs. Sexually active? Declines to discuss today.

Exam: thin, fit young man in no distress. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur standing or squatting, no click. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no spleen tip felt. Joints full range, no laxity. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal.

PHQ-2 0.

Assessment/plan:
- Pre-participation exam: cleared for full participation, form signed. Sickle cell trait documented on the form since the NCAA asks for it.
- Sickle cell trait: talked about why it matters for him as an endurance athlete. Hydrate before, during and after; build up gradually in the heat; stop and tell the trainer if he cramps, feels weak or can't keep up in a way that isn't normal for him. He has heard this before.
- Screening labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HIV and hep C, which he agrees to.
- Will request his old pediatric records and shot history.
- Flu shot when it comes in.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Curtis, all of your blood work from Tuesday is normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good luck with the season.

documents.title: Form for athletic training
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, the athletic trainer says they need the physical form plus something separate that says I have sickle cell trait, they want it on file. Can you send that? Thanks

documents.title: RE: Form for athletic training
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Curtis, the doctor signed a short letter confirming your trait status. Both the letter and your completed physical form are uploaded to your portal under Letters so you can forward them. Let us know if the trainer needs them faxed instead.

documents.title: Pediatric records, prior practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from patient's former pediatric office (14 pages), scanned.

Summary per their last well visit (age 18): healthy, sickle cell trait on newborn hemoglobin screen, no hospitalizations. Immunization record attached: childhood series complete; Tdap 2014; HPV two-dose series 2014 and 2015; MenACWY 2014 and booster 2018; COVID primary series spring 2021 (pharmacy). Immunizations entered.

PCP initials on review.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after practice for vaccines. Feeling well, no fever. No prior reactions. Flu vaccine L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. VIS given. Sat 15 min, fine, left for dinner. Told him his arm may be sore for a run or two.

documents.title: Health form for summer job
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I got a summer job as a camp counselor and they need a health form with my immunizations. Can I just get a copy of my shot record from you guys or does it have to be filled out by the doctor?

documents.title: RE: Health form for summer job
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Curtis, an immunization printout is in your portal now. If the camp form needs a physician signature, upload it here and we'll complete it from your August physical. No visit needed.

documents.title: RE: Health form for summer job
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Uploaded it. Thank you!

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o runner back for his yearly physical and team form. Says the year went fine, ran the whole season without injury, spent the summer working at a day camp and running on his own.

ROS negative: no exertional chest pain, syncope, palpitations, wheeze, muscle cramping, dark urine.

Meds none. NKDA. Sickle cell trait, no problems from it. No tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: well, vitals as charted, resting pulse runner-slow. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. MSK normal, no tenderness over shins or feet. Skin normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Pre-participation: cleared, form completed and uploaded.
2. Sickle cell trait: same heat and hydration talk as last year. Team has a cooling tub at meets now, he says.
3. CBC today since he asked for one for the team dietitian.
4. Flu shot in October.
See you next August.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L deltoid) and 2023-24 COVID (R deltoid) given. Well today, no reactions in the past. Observed 15 minutes. Asked to schedule his physical for next August before preseason.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Curtis, 22, here for his yearly exam and the athletics form. Senior-year season starting in two weeks, first race early September. Ran a lot of the summer in the heat at home. Feels strong.

No syncope or near-syncope, no chest pain, no cramping episodes, no dark urine. Sleeping fine. Mood good.
Meds: none. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.
Family history unchanged (father with sickle trait, mother HTN, paternal uncle T2DM).

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. Cardiac regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Normal gait and strength.

A/P
- Cleared for cross-country, form signed with trait status noted.
- Sickle cell trait: reviewed again, early-season heat is the risky stretch; drink on a schedule, back off if anything feels off.
- Tdap due (last 2014), given today.
- CMP today, he wanted his kidney numbers checked since he trains hard.
- Flu shot in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Curtis, your metabolic panel came back normal, kidney function and electrolytes included. Have a good season.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, brief clinical note (sent to PCP)
Date of service: 09/07/2024

22M collegiate cross-country runner, EMS from a race course. Went down abruptly near the end of a race on a hot, humid afternoon. Per teammates and coach, before he fell he had been very dizzy, complaining of a pounding headache and had vomited, then was stumbling. Patient himself could not give a history on arrival: lethargic, at times agitated.

Known sickle cell trait per team paperwork. No meds. NKDA.

Arrival vitals: T 40.2 C, HR 158, BP 96/58, RR 26.
Exam: hot, flushed skin, dry, no sweating. No focal neuro deficit. No seizure activity observed.

Course: airway protected and circulation supported, rapid cooling begun on arrival, IV fluid resuscitation. Mentation cleared as core temp came down. Labs notable for mild transaminase elevation and an elevated CK. Kept in ED observation overnight on fluids, tolerating PO and ambulating at discharge.

Impression: exertional heat stroke; rhabdomyolysis.
Disposition: home with teammate. Rest, fluids, no running until seen by PCP with repeat labs within 1-2 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ER on Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I passed out at my race Saturday and ended up in the ER overnight. They said it was heat stroke and my muscle enzyme was high. They gave me IV fluids and cooled me down. I feel ok now just really sore and tired. They told me to get bloodwork and see you before I run again. When can I come in?

documents.title: RE: ER on Saturday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry to hear that, Curtis, glad you are feeling better. We have you on the schedule Tuesday 9/17 at 10:30, which gives the labs time to settle. Please keep drinking fluids and rest until then. If your urine turns dark like cola, you have trouble making urine, or you get confused or faint, go back to the ER. We have asked the hospital to send their note.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for heat stroke

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his ED visit 9/7 for exertional heat stroke with rhabdo. ED note reviewed (no lab values in it: transaminases mildly up, CK elevated). Collapsed late in a race on a humid day; does not remember the last part of the course or the ambulance. Cooled and fluid-resuscitated, observed overnight.

Since then: sore legs for about 4 days, now gone. Urine never dark that he noticed. No headache, no confusion, eating and drinking normally. Has not run. Wants to know when he can race.

Exam: well, vitals as charted. Alert and oriented, thinking clearly. Heart regular, lungs clear. Thighs and calves nontender, strength 5/5, no swelling. Neuro nonfocal, normal gait and tandem.

Labs drawn this morning before the visit: CMP normal including AST, ALT and creatinine; CK normal.

A/P
1. Exertional heat stroke, recovered. Rhabdomyolysis, resolved by labs. Sickle cell trait likely contributed along with the conditions that day.
2. Return to running: graded, over about two weeks, starting with short easy runs in cool parts of the day, supervised by the team's athletic trainer, no racing until he has done a full week of normal training without symptoms. Will send the trainer a letter.
3. Reviewed early warning signs again and the plan to stop, cool and tell someone. Fluids on a schedule.
Call with any symptoms.

documents.title: Letter to athletic training staff
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the athletic training staff:

Curtis Grant is under my care. He was treated on 9/7/2024 for exertional heat stroke with rhabdomyolysis. He has recovered and his follow-up blood work, including CK and kidney function, is normal. He has sickle cell trait.

He may begin a graded return to running under your supervision: easy, short sessions at cooler times of day, increasing over about two weeks as tolerated, with free access to fluids and rest. No competition until he has completed a full normal training week without symptoms. Please stop activity and contact me for any recurrence of dizziness, headache, cramping, weakness or dark urine.

Sincerely,
Primary care physician

documents.title: Letter for your trainer
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Curtis, the letter for the athletic trainer is in your portal under Letters.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu shot L deltoid, tolerated. Offered the 2024-25 COVID vaccine, he'd rather skip it this year. Back to racing, says it's going ok. 15 min observation, no issues.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN NOTE, regional hospital, copy to primary care
Visit 06/07/2025

CC: collapse at outdoor concert.

22-year-old with sickle cell trait and a history of exertional heat stroke last September. Brought in by friends from an all-day outdoor music festival; it was 38 C out. Friends say he had been dancing for hours with no breaks and drank very little water before he went down.

Vitals on arrival: T 41.0 C, HR 130, BP 90/60, RR 24.
Exam: disoriented, agitated. Skin hot and dry.

Labs: Na 145, K 4.2, creatinine 1.8, BUN 20. CK 10,000. PT 14 sec, INR 1.2, PTT 35 sec. Lactate 5.

Treatment: rapid cooling, aggressive IV fluids. Mental status normalized with cooling. Monitored overnight in ED observation on IV fluids, urine output good, discharged next afternoon.

Dx: heat stroke (exertional), rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury.
Follow up with PCP for repeat CK and kidney function in about a week. Return for dark urine, low urine output, confusion.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Patient call after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called. Was at a music festival Saturday, collapsed, friends took him to the ED. Told it was heat stroke again plus kidney strain and high muscle enzymes. Got fluids overnight, home Sunday afternoon. Today feels washed out, thighs sore, urine is light yellow, drinking well. No confusion, no fever.
Plan: f/u with PCP 6/17 with labs that morning (BMP, CK). Return precautions given (dark urine, little urine, confusion, vomiting). Requested ED records.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u 6/7 ED visit. Second heat stroke, this time not at a race: outdoor festival on a very hot day, hours of dancing, little water. ED note in: T 41, HR 130, BP 90/60; Cr 1.8, BUN 20, CK 10,000, lactate 5, coags essentially normal (INR 1.2). Cooled, IV fluids, overnight obs.

He is a little embarrassed about it. Soreness gone by Thursday. Urine normal color. Energy back. No headaches.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, oriented, normal speech. Heart and lungs normal. Muscles nontender, full strength. Neuro nonfocal.

Labs this morning: BMP normal with creatinine back to his usual; CK normal.

A/P
1. Exertional heat stroke, second episode (first 9/2024), recovered.
2. Rhabdo and AKI, resolved on today's labs.
3. Sickle cell trait in a young man who has now had two heat strokes nine months apart. Long talk: hot days count even when it isn't a race; water on a schedule, shade and breaks; leave the crowd early if he starts feeling dizzy or headachy; tell friends what to watch for. He gets it.
4. Summer training: ok to resume easy running at cool times now that labs are normal, and let the athletic trainer know before fall preseason.
Physical in August as usual.

documents.title: Reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt left a message, has a team meeting tomorrow morning, needs to move his physical. Moved to Tue 8/19 8:30. Confirmed by text.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M, yearly visit and team paperwork. Fall season starts in two weeks.

Interval: heat stroke x2 (race 9/2024; festival 6/2025 with rhabdo and AKI that resolved). Since June: running easy then building, no symptoms, has been doing his longer runs at 6 am. No dizziness, cramping or dark urine. Drinking well.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
FHx: father sickle trait, mother hypertension, paternal uncle with type 2 DM.

Exam: vitals as charted, looks well. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. MSK and neuro normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Pre-participation: cleared, with the heat stroke history and sickle cell trait written on the form so the athletic trainer has it. Spoke with him about the team's heat plan: acclimatize over the first two weeks, scheduled fluids, a cold tub at practices and meets, he stops at the first sign of trouble.
- Labs: CBC and CMP today.
- Flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and chemistry panel are both normal, kidney function included. Your physical form is in the portal.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great thanks!!

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine R deltoid. Declined COVID again. Well, no reactions. Waited the 15 minutes.

documents.title: Spring track form?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Do I need a new physical for spring track or does the one from August count? The trainer wasn't sure.

documents.title: RE: Spring track form?
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Curtis, the August pre-participation exam covers the whole academic year, so no new visit is needed. If the trainer wants a fresh signature on their spring form, upload it and we will sign from the August exam.

reports.text: Noncontrast axial images of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No extra-axial collection. Calvarium intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Internal Medicine service. Discharge summary (brief), faxed to primary care.
Admitted 04/14/2026, discharged 04/16/2026.

Reason for admission: witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home.

HPI: 23-year-old man with sickle cell trait and exertional heat stroke in 2024 and again in 2025. Roommate saw him have a convulsion lasting about 3 minutes this morning, after which he was confused for a while. EMS transport. He reports no recent illness. No medications. Denies alcohol or drug use.

Admission vitals: T 37.2 C, BP 135/85, P 88, RR 16.
Exam: awake and alert, tired-appearing. Neurologic exam without focal findings.

Data: CK 20,000 U/L. Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. Potassium 5.5 mEq/L. UA: SG 1.025, pH 6.0, blood 3+, protein 1+, no RBCs seen on microscopy (pattern consistent with myoglobinuria). CT head without contrast: no acute intracranial abnormality.

Hospital course: no further seizures. Treated with IV fluids for rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury, with improvement in CK and creatinine before discharge. Not started on an antiseizure medication.

Discharge diagnoses: seizure; rhabdomyolysis; acute kidney injury.
Discharge medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within a week with repeat CK and BMP. Outpatient neurology evaluation. Seizure precautions and Massachusetts driving restriction reviewed.

documents.title: Post-discharge scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called from home, discharged from the hospital today after a seizure. They want him seen this week with labs. Scheduled tomorrow 4/17 at 2:00 with PCP. Roommate is driving him. Asked him to bring all discharge paperwork.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 1 day after discharge. Admitted 4/14-4/16 after a seizure at home. Full summary not here yet; going from his discharge instructions and his account.

He woke up on the floor with EMTs in the room. Roommate told him it was a whole-body shaking episode, about 3 minutes, then he was out of it for a while after. No warning he can recall. Had not been sick. No alcohol, no drugs, no new supplements, nothing missed. Never had a seizure before, none as a child.

Discharge paperwork: CK 20,000 and creatinine 1.8 on arrival, potassium a little high; CT of the head normal; IV fluids; no seizure medicine started; neurology to see him as an outpatient.

Today: tired, thighs still sore. Urine clear and normal amount. No headache, no further spells, no confusion.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, oriented x3, conversational, normal recall of today's events. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Thighs mildly tender, strength 5/5. Neuro: cranial nerves intact, no drift, reflexes symmetric, finger-nose and gait normal.

A/P
1. Seizure, first, generalized tonic-clonic per witness. Cause not clear. Referred to neurology (discharge plan). Safety: no driving for 6 months from 4/14 per state rules, no swimming or bathing alone, no climbing or heights, roommate knows to time any event and call 911 if more than 5 minutes.
2. Rhabdomyolysis and AKI with this admission (CK 20,000, Cr 1.8). Repeat CK and BMP next Friday. No running or lifting until those are back normal. Fluids.
3. Sickle cell trait, history of exertional heat stroke x2 (2024, 2025).
Will message him with the lab results. Requested the full hospital summary.

events.reason: Repeat CK and BMP after admission

documents.title: Lab results from today
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Curtis, good news: your CK (the muscle enzyme) is back to normal, and your kidney function and potassium are normal too. You can start easing back into light activity. Driving and the other seizure precautions still stand until you've seen neurology and the 6 months have passed.

documents.title: neurology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neurology called, the first new patient spot they have is September 9. Is that ok or should I be trying to get in sooner? No more seizures.

documents.title: RE: neurology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: September is a long wait but reasonable since you have had only the one seizure and are doing well. Ask them to put you on their cancellation list. If anything happens again before then, call us or go to the ER.

documents.title: Running this summer
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I've been doing easy runs early in the morning with a friend and feel totally normal. Coach is asking about fall. Am I ok to train normally or do I have to wait for neurology?

documents.title: RE: Running this summer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Easy running with a partner, early in the day and well hydrated, is fine. I'd hold off on full training and any competition until neurology has seen you in September; then we'll do your fall physical and team form together. Keep running with company for now, not solo on trails.

documents.title: Sept appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neurology is still Sept 9, no cancellations came up. Also can I get my flu shot at the campus clinic this year? Easier with my schedule.

documents.title: RE: Sept appointment
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, that's fine. Just send us the date and the vaccine name when you get it so we can add it to your record. Please book your physical for after the neurology visit.
